groups.label: Purity in Music and Law
groups.summary: Socrates establishes standards for purging luxury and vice from the city by restricting musical instruments to simple forms and requiring that judges maintain incorruptible minds unsoiled by early experience of wickedness.
groups.rationale: Both passages from Book III address cultural and institutional safeguards designed to preserve uncorrupted simplicity in the civic community.

groups.label: Selection of the Rulers
groups.summary: Socrates details the selection and testing of elder guardians through severe trials, distinguishes them from younger auxiliaries, and introduces the foundational myth of metals to justify meritocratic class divisions.
groups.rationale: These four consecutive Book III sections formulate the hierarchy, trial procedures, and governing myth for the guardian ruling class.

groups.label: Guardians and Warfare
groups.summary: Socrates outlines the five civic constitutions and soul types, mandates equal education and duties for female guardians, institutes collective mating and kinship, and limits warfare practices among Hellenic cities.
groups.rationale: Covers constitutional foundations and the communal, educational, and external military regulations established across Books IV and V.

groups.label: Nature of True Philosophers
groups.summary: True philosophers are characterized by their passion for the whole of wisdom and the vision of truth, contrasting with superficial sight-lovers and the base imitators who corrupt philosophy when genuine seekers depart.
groups.rationale: These passages define genuine philosophy in Books V and VI against amateur dilettantes and unworthy imitators.

groups.label: Oligarchy and Democracy
groups.summary: Socrates defines oligarchy based on wealth and property valuation, then describes democracy's chaotic personal freedom, varied constitutions, and internal division into three distinct economic classes.
groups.rationale: These Book VIII sections examine the defective constitutional forms of oligarchy and democracy and their internal class structures.

groups.label: Editorial Analyses of Plato
groups.summary: Editorial paratext evaluates Plato's aesthetic criteria of moderation and censorship alongside his implementation of communal property and family structures to foster civic unity.
groups.rationale: Both entries consist of editorial commentary analyzing thematic motifs (artistic censorship and communism) across the dialogues.
